docs.title: About this book
docs.text:
The first book to apply the new theory of evolution to human origins: an account of the natural history of the man-like apes, a comparison of their anatomy and development with that of man, and an examination of the fossil skulls then known, including the Neanderthal.

From Wikisource · Public domain

Thomas Henry Huxley (1825–1895), Evidence as to Man's Place in Nature, London, Williams and Norgate, 1863; text from Wikisource. This book is not stored in this library: each chapter is read from Wikisource when it is opened, shown in this library's format, and ends with its own attribution. Licence: Public domain.
